changed.what: N24ap1-01 leaves the step group scorecard-oracle-* of scripts/e2e/arena_scorecards.sh to this bead. If it stayed out, nobody would ever check the scorecard's fixture-record infeasibility (body 0.62 m, doorway 0.55 m) against the oracle. Added the group to Scope and to the e2e plan: the command, a synthetic legality profile that admits 0.55 m (a default profile's 0.70 to 0.90 m would answer 360), the assertions, the log and the control oracle-point-robot. Also added an acceptance criterion and dep N24ap1-01 (M1; no cycle).

Technical approach listed 'seeds (64), threshold (48)' as options. They are N26a-17's fixed constants and are not on the VERBS-nemesis row. An implementer would add inputs the row lacks, so the help snapshot would fail, and a caller could loosen what 'fails' means. The options are now restated as the row spells them (--max-tests, --no-pair-check, --tier, --out, key, budget).

The surface used `frob nemesis audit prepare|run <campaign>` and a request schema whose action could be 'prepare' or 'run'. Under NJL-01 action rule 1 both forms are FROB-REF-802 (a positional action word; a name for the default), so the verb as written would fail its help snapshot and the parity checks. Applied M1-5: --action prepare; the default run has no name; the offline form has no action word; the schema's one action value is prepare; the acceptance criterion and unit test now assert the 802 cases.

Line 50 used the positional audit forms, which are 802 under NJL-01, so every audit call of the script would fail. Restated as --action prepare, the default action and the offline form. Step 6's second `prepare` had no key of its own: reusing na-6p-0 would replay the stored commitment instead of answering not-run, which fails the assertion. It now uses na-6p2-0.

Step 8's bound call lacked --finalist. The finalists-only rule refuses rare-bound-not-finalist before the lane firewall's 560 (N26a-26, N10a-09), so the 560 assertion could never pass; the flag is added. Step 8's qualify probe ('offer one covering item') named no input that can carry it; it is now `--clusters covering` (N24b-16's 567 case). GATE-NEMESIS-08's controls no-remaining-term, top-one-gain and the lazy queue without its stamp check had no registrant under BD-025, so the gate would have listed unregistered controls and stayed ineligible at M3. This bead, which measures the gate, now appends their GATE-NEMESIS-08-seeded records.

Fixes in this bead: (1) The audit forms now use --action (M1-5). (2) Rows 360 to 362 went through `search --method given`, which completes and lists `refused` (BD-273), so they never exited 3; they now go through `nemesis oracle`, which refuses the request in step 1. (3) Bound calls lacked --tier (required) and --finalist, so every bound row would answer rare-bound-not-finalist; both are now required, with one exception. (4) The 760 row assumed a 100% nominal share, but under `table` the share is 80% and the 300,000 twin would be refused; the assertions now follow the share the record names, and the twin is 375,000. (5) The 568 row re-used a key after the task edit, which gives 803 (N32a-09), not 568; it is now a new request offering the old episodes. (6) The 567 twin named sealed worlds, which is 567 again; `clusters` is now a count. (7) Step 7's 569 fallback exists only while the table policy acts; it now runs under a scratch `nemesis.bound.policy = table`. (8) The audit not-run situation needs the M4 verb; it is now recorded `not run` before M4 (convention 7).

Three changes. Added dep N26b-16: the acceptance criterion binds each obligation to its derivation file, which N26b-16 writes (both M3, no cycle). The bead called the eight mutant features 'the rows of N26-CX', but only lane-open (CX-290) and guard-off (CX-295) are entry plants; the other six would have had no control record, so the 'registry lists all eight' criterion could not pass. This bead now appends six INV-NEMESIS-nn-seeded records under BD-025 (gates by rule_gates; GATE-NEMESIS-01 for broken-legality and oracle-skip-guard), with nc_ tests. The e2e section now says why no script is owed (C11).

The KA-664 surface command (nemesis bound quad-tray … --estimate) had no --finalist, so it would be refused with rare-bound-not-finalist. It also had no budget, so the printed count depended on a default budget and on the acting policy (sequential at 92,872 versus fixed-n at 29,956). Added --finalist and --budget episodes=50000; that budget gives fixed-n at 29,956 under either policy.

C13: the bead narrated 'listed pending until that bead registers it' and 'GATE-NEMESIS-02 until BD-273 registers its potency control'. No bead registers those controls, and the potency control belongs to N26a-11, not BD-273, so the gates would stay pending forever unnoticed. It now states BD-025's rule as fact and names each registrant: N26b-15 (INV seeds), and N26a-11, N26a-34, N26a-31, N26a-16 and N26b-12 (GATE seeds), with requests filed to the four outside the slice. The acceptance check is restated as 'a gate with a pending control is ineligible'. C9 is a false alarm: the bead writes the controls and tier fields, never a measurement.

The e2e expected `nemesis search … --require-cited` to exit 3 with 361. Under BD-273, search confines its proposals to cited or card quantities and refuses only when none remain, so the first assertion would fail on any kitchen profile with a card bound. The 361 probe and its synthetic-source follow-up now use `nemesis oracle` on the trap world, which refuses when a touched bound is assumed. Search calls (ls-3, ls-4) are kept for the shares and for the confined search.

The crude arm `nemesis bound … --mode estimate` lacked --finalist. A fixture candidate is no finalist of a recorded campaign, so every crude-arm run would be refused and the experiment would have no baseline arm. Added --finalist.

Fixes in this bead: (1) Bound calls lacked --finalist, so each would be refused rare-bound-not-finalist. (2) There was no budget, so 760 could stand in for the envelope refusal; --budget episodes=3750000 now covers 2,995,731 under either share. (3) ne-4 named an approved R5 scope but did not cite it. Without --envelope-scope a request's scope is adhoc (E0) and it is still refused (convention 14, NJL-01); ne-4, step 5 and the acceptance criterion now cite it. (4) A daemon-queued campaign-class job gets 704 from the size classifier, not 761 (N36-20, convention 14), so the ne-2 assertion now admits either, with each one's repairs.

Every bound call of the e2e lacked --finalist and would be refused. The 10⁻⁴ case at a budget of 100,000 routes to the sibling's sequence only when the whole budget is the nominal share. Under `table` the share is 80,000, below the sequence's 92,872, so the route becomes exact and the acceptance criterion and e2e would fail once the policy is adopted. The budget is now 120,000 (96,000 under table), and the unit test states both shares.

H-owners-3: the bead spelled the hardset actions as sub-commands (`hardset carry`, `hardset show`, `carry --refresh`), which NJL-01 refuses with 802, so the action and its script would be unreachable as written. Restated as --action carry (and --action add, the default show) in Scope, the command, --refresh, the acceptance criteria, the unit test and the e2e.

The bound calls lacked --finalist and would be refused. The budgets 1,200,000 (meant to route 10⁻⁵ to the sequence) and 3·10⁶ (for the 10⁻⁶ certification) work only when the whole budget is the nominal share. Under `table` (80%), which acts at M4 after adoption, the first routes to fixed-n and the second is refused with 760. They are now 1,350,000 and 3,750,000 in the e2e, procedure step 7 and the routing unit test, and procedure step 4 speaks of the nominal share.

requests.what: State the user-side request that reaches admission rule 3 (FROB-REF-568), and the order in which rules 1 to 4 are checked. For example: a new bound on an edited task offered, through --episodes, nominal episodes recorded under the old predicate; and whether such an offered set's addresses fall in the new commitment's range. Without this, an offered set may be refused 560 by rule 1 or 2 before rule 3 is reached. N26b-14's 568 row and N26a-30's step 9 rely on it.

Register GATE-NEMESIS-02's controls that no catalogue entry or KA row states (the potency control and the A/A arm the gate register names) as records of controls.toml with BD-025's GATE-NEMESIS-02 seed. N26b-18 now names this bead as their registrant; without the records the gate stays ineligible.

Register GATE-NEMESIS-03's unseeded controls with BD-025's GATE-NEMESIS-03 seed: the first-round-only shrinker (nemesis-shrink-first-round-only) and the planted file with one altered digest. N26b-18 names this bead as their registrant.
Register GATE-NEMESIS-05's crude-sampling baseline arm, which N26b-18's row names as a control, with BD-025's GATE-NEMESIS-05 seed (or state why it is no control record).

Resolve nemesis-guard-reject-all (BD-272) against KA-662's seeded control ('a genuine planted failure survives every variant'). If no seeded record states it, register it with BD-025's GATE-NEMESIS-06 seed, as N26b-18 now says.

Declare a test feature for the planted lazy queue that skips its stamp check (N26b-12 now registers it as nemesis-cover-mut-lazy-no-stamp, a GATE-NEMESIS-08 control); N26b-09 states the defect but names no feature.

Line 60 says a campaign-class job without an approved class is refused at submission by the envelope stage with FROB-REF-761. Convention 14 and N36-20 give FROB-REF-704 from the size classifier at submission and 704 again at dispatch on a lapsed approval. Align the row of the size-class table.
